# Map-Not-Encyclopedia Doctrine (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.14.0` — the rule also loads on the canon it governs (`.gzkit/corpus/**`, `.gzkit/rules/**`, `.gzkit/skills/**`), since the three generated surfaces are never edited by hand (RP-7 held ruling H13, operator, 2026-11-14: *"A: Keep, re-scope"*); version narrative in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#agents-md-map-doctrinemd).

## Invariant

AGENTS.md MUST contain only (a) binding bullet rules (one bullet = one rule, ≤ 3 lines per bullet), (b) structured tables (Persona, Gate Covenant, OBPI kinds, canonical invocations, defect-fix routing thresholds), and (c) canonical-link references to deeper documentation at stable URLs under `docs/governance/`. AGENTS.md MUST NOT contain (i) multi-paragraph rationale prose (a paragraph over 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor), (ii) worked examples or anti-pattern catalogs, (iii) "Why this is canon" / "Why X" coda blockquotes, (iv) narrative pedagogical sections, or (v) operative-claims expansions whose binding-bullet form already states the rule. CLAUDE.md inherits the same shape contract; `.claude/rules/*.md` inherit it with their per-file budget.

## Budget

The enforced budgets are the values in `data/instructions_files_budget.json`, read by `gz validate --instructions-files-budget`; this rule never restates them (a duplicated number drifts from what is enforced — the drift ADR-0.0.54 closeout corrected). The destination for AGENTS.md is the range in `docs/governance/agents-md-doctrine.md` § Budget targets, an ideal and a ceiling (operator rulings 2026-09-19); closing the distance lands under `ADR-0.35.0-canon-entry-corpus-landing` § Decision 3 (sections declare `corpus-owned` or `unowned`, the generator materializes owned sections, the unowned byte total is a decrease-only ratchet). Cite that ADR directly; its predecessors (`ADR-0.0.37`, GHI #533) are terminal.

Budgets are advisory until 1.0 (operator ruling 2026-08-17): every file is measured and each overrun reported with its distance and the `/gz-context-diet` pointer, but nothing blocks. The Codex delivery cap in `data/vendor-manifest.json` is a limit gzkit **sets** through the `.codex/config.toml` it generates, and any change to it is verified by observing what Codex actually delivered — `gz validate --instructions-files-budget` carries a codex-delivery witness for that (GHI #962). Raising the cap without re-observing delivery is the defect GHI #815 recorded.

## Shape enforcement

`gz validate --agents-md-map-conformance` asserts, fail-closed: no paragraph in AGENTS.md over 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor; no subsection title in the prohibited set; every `See [text](path)` link resolves. File size is reported against the budget file, advisory only. Violations emit a `RemediationPayload` with `recovery: /gz-context-diet`.

Bringing an over-budget surface back into trim is the `instructions-files-diet` chore's job, on a cadence or on demand; ordinary sessions add to sources (`gz content remember`) and never resize a render surface.

## Attestation granularity

Operator ruling 2026-08-17: **the discriminator is whether CANON changed — never whether a file was written.** A rendition is a Layer-3 derived view; the corpus is Layer-1. Attestation attaches to the canon change and to completed OBPI/ADR work, never to the projection.

| Act | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Re-render of **unchanged** canon | No attestation; the corpus fingerprint is unmoved and `--rendition-floor-coherence` proves the invariant floor survived. The chore completes it. |
| Adding a corpus entry (`gz content remember`) | Attested — recorded provenance |
| Removing an entry (`gz content retire`) | Attested — recorded provenance |
| Trim / compression to fit a delivery cap | Invites operator review: it changes what canon looks like, not what canon is |

- A GHI needs no attestation (operator verbatim: *"I only attest to completed obpi/adr work"*); the GHI is the work order and the receipt.
- Do not call a build step "Gate 5." The content surface's attestation is named CORPUS ATTESTATION. Gate 5 is OBPI/ADR completion attestation (ADR-0.0.36) and nothing else; the noun is `corpus`, not `rendition`, because the attestable subject is the corpus (GHI #822).
- Attestation on add/remove is recorded provenance, never a blocking gate: *"Capture must never be blocked: losing the operator's words is strictly worse than a red tree"* (`ADR-0.35.0` § Decision 7).
- The transport never gates the attestation: a ruling relayed verbatim via `--attestation-text` IS the attestation; "the operator is not at a terminal" never stops a chore.

(Advisory — no witness holds it, and the verbs carry the granularity only in part: `gz content remember` takes no `--attestor`, only a `--witness` recorded as provenance; `gz content retire` requires `--attestor` only when the retirement moves invariant-tier liveness; `gz content commit` requires `--attestor` and `--attestation-text` only when the corpus moved since that consumer's last committed rendition (GHI #821). Reclassify when the verbs carry the granularity.)

## Writing levers

Apply these when writing or trimming an `AGENTS.md` corpus entry, `CLAUDE.md`, a rule or a skill description. (Advisory — whether a sentence steers is settled by running the surface, not by reading it.)

- **Two loads.** Always-loaded text costs context on every turn; material behind a pointer costs the operator the memory that it exists. Spend context on what every task needs.
- **Branch test.** Inline what every task needs; put what only some tasks reach behind a pointer (a path-scoped rule, a skill, a doc). A rule that must steer every turn stays inline in full.
- **Pointer wording.** A pointer says what the material is and when to reach it. When a needed target is being missed, sharpen the pointer before inlining the material.
- **Positive target.** State the behavior wanted; keep a prohibition only as a hard guardrail with no positive phrasing, paired with the target.
- **No-op hunt.** A sentence the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing; delete it. The default is model-relative, so a disagreement is settled by a run.
- **Single source, and the environment counts.** One home per meaning. Restating what a config file, `--help` or the directory layout already says is a cache that goes stale; keep the convention, the reason, the gotcha.
- **Co-location.** A concept's rule, its caveats and its witness sit under one heading.
- **Leading words.** Reuse gzkit's established terms (witness, canon, derived view, coupled surface, direct fix) as tokens; do not re-explain them.
- **A skill description is a pointer that never unloads.** A skill the agent need not reach on its own is user-invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`) and costs no context.

## Related

- `docs/governance/agents-md-doctrine.md` — canonical expansion; `docs/governance/agent-contract-rationale.md` — lift target
- `.gzkit/skills/gz-context-diet/SKILL.md` — the operator-facing procedure; `data/instructions_files_budget.json` — the enforced values
- `ADR-0.0.54-agents-md-map-not-encyclopedia-doctrine` — parent ADR

# Mode Contract (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.1.2` — the fail-safe default restored after the 0.1.1 compression (operator review, 2026-10-28); advisory until RO-13 lands its witness.

Every new control, module, skill, rule or surface carries the two-way mode contract from its first commit: operator, 2026-10-26, *"an overarching design requirement permanently and always with everything we build"*. A design without it is incomplete. Retrofitting what exists is RO-13's program.

## What a new control declares

1. **Its behavior** at the operational condition, the **hangar** level and the **drydock** level: on, advisory or off. The condition is on only when the marker is present, parses, is bound to an open `mx_session_opened` and is not exiting. Anything else is the operational condition.
2. **Its MEL entry:** level per standby level, (M) bypass procedure, (O) limitation, placard, restore condition and deadline (at the latest the exit re-run), self-test interval, accepted state.
3. **Its built-in self-test:** suitable when its latest result passed within the declared interval, otherwise inoperative under its (O) limitation.

`GATE5_INVARIANTS` is never listed. The level is applied at the place of call, never by the declaration. Until RO-13 builds the declaration shapes (decorator, Markdown MEL block, `gzkit.mx.alarms` arguments), state the contract in the design artifact's § Mode Contract.

**Advisory: no mechanical witness yet.** RO-13's shrink-only baseline of controls with no MEL entry, closed at zero, is the planned witness. Record: `docs/rnd/contractor-kit.md` § *the mode contract is a permanent design requirement for everything gzkit builds*.

# Model Selection (gzkit)

<!-- rule-version: 0.8.1 -->

> **Rule version:** `0.8.1` — the Agent tool now has a per-call `effort` input, so two claims that it takes only `model` and `subagent_type` are corrected (operator, 2026-11-08: *"fix what is stale"*); prior narrative in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#model-selectionmd).

## Operative claims (binding)

1. **Model tier is determined by decision complexity, not task size.** Large read-only tasks use Haiku; small design decisions use Opus.
2. **Default to the lowest tier that closes the decision space.** Each surface must name what "closing the decision" means.
3. **Skill SKILL.md files carry explicit `model:` frontmatter.** No inference; declaration is the contract.
4. **Subagent effort is set on the agent definition, never on the dispatch call.** An agent's `effort:` frontmatter (or the SDK `AgentDefinition.effort`) carries it. The Agent tool's per-call `effort` input is, by its own description, for when the user or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill explicitly ask; this rule does not ask for it. An `effort:` line written into a prompt is text the subagent reads, not a harness control. Agents do not hardcode model IDs.
5. **A subagent's claim is not evidence.** Never relay a subagent's factual assertion into ceremony, attestation, or an operator-facing conclusion on the subagent's word — cite the ARB receipt, the file, or re-run the command yourself. The orchestrator owns every claim it passes upward.

## Routing matrix

| Work Type | Model | Decision space | Example |
|-----------|-------|-----------------|---------|
| **Read-only search/lookup** | Haiku | None—pattern matching only | Explore agent finding files by grep, Bash read operations |
| **Mechanical validation** | Haiku | Binary (pass/fail); no tradeoff analysis | `gz register-adrs` checking ADR frontmatter, `gz validate` gates |
| **Routine code review** | Haiku | Bounded checklist; style/naming only | Linting output, pre-commit hook errors, simple ruff/typecheck fixes |
| **Format normalization** | Haiku | Deterministic transformation | YAML/JSON reformatting, table rendering, template instantiation |
| **Architectural design, planning** | Opus | Unbounded; constraints compete; novel decisions | ADR authoring, `/gz-design`, brief writing, cross-surface coherence checks |
| **Complex refactoring** | Opus | Dataflow reasoning across N≥3 files | Multi-file renames, schema migrations, coupled-surface updates |
| **Gate-5 attestation, narrative synthesis** | Opus | Operator-facing quality; tone and completeness matter | Closing OBPIs with evidence, writing release notes, operator-facing prose |
| **Mythos-class judgment (operator-supervised)** | Fable | Highest-stakes judgment; doctrine and evidence evaluation | System-card evaluation, doctrine refresh, design dialogues, adversarial review sessions |
| **Subagent multi-step work** | Varies (see below) | Depends on subtask type | Agent spawned for parallel exploration, verification, or specialized review |

## Skill frontmatter (`model:` directive)

Every skill SKILL.md MUST declare the model tier used when invoking the skill runtime:

```yaml
---
metadata:
  skill-version: "0.1.0"
model: haiku  # or: sonnet, opus
---
# Skill Name

...
```

**Valid values:** `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `fable`. No inference; no runtime detection; declared value is the contract. `fable` is reserved for Mythos-class judgment surfaces (operator-supervised); pipelines and mechanical work never default to it.

**Canon names a Claude model by class, never by a versioned ID.** The harness resolves the class to that class's current model at dispatch. A versioned model ID goes stale at the next launch, so rule, skill and agent canon never carries one (operator ruling 2026-10-26, verbatim: "cleary we should use class of model, not specific version"; GHI #1284). Fail-closed by `gz validate --model-class-only` over `.gzkit/rules/`, `.gzkit/skills/` and `.gzkit/agents/`. Records that name the model which did a piece of work — the ledger, handoffs, `data/frontier_model_cards.json` — stay exact.

## Subagent effort levels

**Where effort is set.** On the agent definition: `.claude/agents/<name>.md` frontmatter `effort:` (documented values `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; default inherits the session's) or the SDK `AgentDefinition.effort`. The Agent tool also takes a per-call `effort` input (`low` to `max`; ignored for a fork), whose description reads *"Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask"* (Agent tool schema, read 2026-11-08). A prompt-level `effort:` directive has no mechanical effect. (Claude Code documentation, read 2026-10-06; `docs/rnd/renewing-vows/sources/` and the run record's source entry *Claude Code documentation on subagent effort*.) Today every definition under `.claude/agents/` carries `model: inherit` and no `effort:`, so every subagent runs at the session's effort.

**The allocation, by echelon and role** (operator ruling 2026-10-05, verbatim *"A (so model + effort)"*; advisory until agent definitions carry `effort:` and the dispatch record names which definition flew):

| Echelon / role | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Headquarters synthesis; the constraints sortie | strongest available (`opus`, or `fable` where Mythos-class judgment is the surface) | `high` |
| Elicitation (interviews, intake) | mid-tier | `low` to `medium` |
| Execution sorties (implementer red and green) | mid-tier | `low` |
| Assessment (spec and quality review) | strong | `high` |
| Cross-vendor IV&V; security-sensitive assessment | strongest | `max` |
| The regeneration test | mid-tier | `low` |

**Rule:** give a subagent the effort needed to close its decision, not the effort that would be "nice to have"; set it on the definition, and define one agent per role × effort band where the bands differ.

## Do Not

- Declaring `model: opus` for a read-only task (use Haiku)
- Defaulting subagents to `effort: xhigh` when `effort: low` would suffice
- Writing `effort: high` into a subagent prompt and expecting the harness to honour it (set it on the definition)
- Hardcoding a model ID (`claude-<tier>-<n>`) in a subagent prompt or dispatch call; pass the tier alias in `model` and set effort on the definition
- Omitting the `model:` directive from a skill and inferring it at runtime
- Using Sonnet as a "middle ground" between Haiku and Opus without naming what decision complexity requires it

See [Model-Selection Rationale](../../docs/governance/model-selection-rationale.md) for context and token economy reasoning.

# Skill Authoring (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.2.1` — version narrative lifted to [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#skill-authoringmd); binding rules unchanged.

Skills are canonical files, not corpus constructed (`docs/governance/agent-control-surface-rendering-substrate.md` § Binding claim), so review is their control. This rule is the standard three chores read, each in its own class: `skill-authoring-quality` checks conformance to it, `instructions-files-diet` curates bodies against § Parsimony, and `frontier-model-card-currency` re-sources wording against § Model alignment. Versioning and sync mechanics are `skill-surface-sync.md`; the `model:` field is `model-selection.md`.

## What a skill carries

- **Procedure plus the judgment a step needs:** which `gz` verb, in what order, what stops the run, what the operator decides. A skill that wraps one command and adds no judgment is an alias: make it user-invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`) or remove it.
- **A one-line description that says when to reach for the skill and what it produces.** It is the only part loaded every turn (`agents-md-map-doctrine.md` § Writing levers).
- **Where it ends.** Every skill states its terminal state and what it does not do.

## Parsimony (binding)

1. **Procedure stays; history leaves.** Dated incident narrative, regression stories and version notes go to a rationale doc under `docs/governance/` or a `references/` file beside the skill. The body keeps one sentence of reason and the pointer.
2. **One home per meaning.** Point at `AGENTS.md`, a rule, `--help` or a model; do not restate them. Text attributed to `AGENTS.md` is quoted from the current file, by section name, or not quoted.
3. **Name the verb, not its work.** Where a `gz` verb scaffolds, validates or books something, the step names the verb; it does not describe doing that work by hand.
4. **Branch test.** Material only some runs reach goes behind a pointer to `references/`.
5. **A rationalization or red-flag row earns its place** by naming a failure observed in this repository for this skill. These tables are not required sections, and a skill is not better for having them.
6. **Size is a finding, and the limit is a trigger to compress.** A body past the threshold `skill-authoring-quality` declares is decomposed or lifted, not excused. Hitting the ceiling is never a licence to grow the surface: search first for compression and consolidation — one meaning restated in two places (clause 2), a rationalization or red-flag row that names no observed failure (clause 5), a section a sibling skill already carries. Lifting to `references/` is the move after that search, not instead of it, and the commit says what was compressed as well as what was lifted. A skill that only ever grows and extracts has not been edited, only relocated.

## Model alignment (binding)

Skill wording follows the current tuning docs, `docs/governance/opus-tuning.md` and `docs/governance/gpt-tuning.md`; cite the doc, never a card. When a card rotates, wording tuned to the old one is up for re-sourcing.

1. **State scope and stop conditions.** Current models widen a task unless told where it ends.
2. **Add no verification or re-check step where a mechanical witness exists** (a test, a hook, `gz check`, a receipt), and no anti-laziness pressure.
3. **Reserve `MUST` and `NEVER` for a constraint the skill itself owns.** A constraint owned elsewhere is cited in plain words.
4. **Keep written constraints.** "Capability gains are not evidence that a written constraint has become less necessary" (`opus-tuning.md` § Recalibration on model change).
5. **State the behavior wanted**; keep a prohibition only as a guardrail paired with its positive target.

## Authority lines a step may not cross

A skill step never instructs what the root contract forbids. The recurring cases, each by its authority:

- initiating, claiming or completing OBPI work — `AGENTS.md` § OBPI Acceptance Protocol;
- `gh issue create` or a bare `gh issue close` — the `ghi-author` and `ghi-close` skills;
- a real name in an attestor field — `AGENTS.md` § Execution Rules;
- treating Gate 5 as lane-dependent — `AGENTS.md` § Gate Covenant;
- a retired command or a path that does not exist — run it and resolve it before writing it.

## Enforcement posture

**Countable body checks plus qualitative review.** `gz skill audit` checks frontmatter, lifecycle, review age, mirror parity, body size and unfinished scaffold markers. Body-size authority is `src/gzkit/skill_contract.py`; packaged cutover ceilings in `src/gzkit/skill_body_grandfather.json` may only shrink or be removed. Existing oversized bodies within their ceilings warn; new oversized bodies and growth beyond a ceiling block. Unfinished active or deprecated bodies block, drafts warn, and retired bodies are excluded. Fenced and quoted examples are excluded from marker detection. `gz validate --cli-alignment` resolves every `gz <verb>` a skill names. `gz validate --skill-alignment` holds every verb to a wielding skill. Qualitative parsimony and model alignment still require judgment: they are judged at authoring and at the three chores above, in propose-rule-land mode, because a repair that touches a skill is operator-only. The countable checks landed under GHI #1037 on 2026-09-19; they do not certify semantic completeness or good decomposition.

# Skill & Surface Sync (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.14.1` — § Surface layout describes the drift report sync actually gives, and the classifier gives `project_local` to skills as well as chores (operator, 2026-11-08: *"fix what is stale"*); prior narrative in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#skill-surface-syncmd).

## Non-negotiable rules

1. **Edit `.gzkit/` first.** `.gzkit/skills/` and `.gzkit/rules/` are canonical; every other copy is generated.
2. **Bump the version on every edit.** Do not edit a skill without bumping its `skill-version` frontmatter, nor a rule without its body-level marker; do not skip sync because two files look the same (it also updates manifests and registrations). Skills: `metadata.skill-version`, a quoted `X.Y.Z` string nested under `metadata:` (a top-level `skill-version:` is invisible to `skills_audit.py`; presence is enforced, `SKA-METADATA-SKILL-VERSION-MISSING`). Rules: the body-level `<!-- rule-version: X.Y.Z -->` comment right after the frontmatter plus the visible `> **Rule version:** \`X.Y.Z\`` block quote with a one-sentence rationale; `RuleFrontmatter` is `extra="forbid"` and rejects `skill-version:` on a rule. Minor for a governance or procedure change, patch for wording or tooling.
3. **Run sync after every edit.** `uv run gz agent sync control-surfaces` writes the wheel copy at `src/gzkit/<surface>/` and every enabled vendor's mirror in one invocation.
4. **Never edit vendor mirrors directly.** Read the roster from `.gzkit.json` § `vendors`, never from a list here — a transcribed roster went stale when Copilot was dropped (GHI #921).
5. **Never edit `src/gzkit/<surface>/` directly.** `src/gzkit/{skills,rules,personas,templates}/` are derived; only `sync_pkg_surfaces` writes them.
6. **`skill-version` bumps require `last_reviewed` bumps in the same edit (skills only).** Set `last_reviewed:` to today's date whenever `skill-version` moves — the 90-day staleness audit (`DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_AGE_DAYS`, `src/gzkit/skills_audit.py`) reads it, and a version bump without it silently disarms that signal. Rules carry no `last_reviewed:`.

## Surface layout

| Canonical (edit here) | Pkg copy (generated) | Vendor mirrors (generated) | Version marker |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.gzkit/skills/` | `src/gzkit/skills/` | `<surface_root>/skills/` per enabled vendor | `metadata.skill-version` |
| `.gzkit/rules/` | `src/gzkit/rules/` | `<surface_root>/rules/` or the vendor's `instruction_format` path | `<!-- rule-version -->` + block quote |
| `.gzkit/personas/` | `src/gzkit/personas/` | `<surface_root>/personas/` | none |
| `.gzkit/templates/` | `src/gzkit/templates/` | none (scaffold-time only) | none |
| `.gzkit/chores/<slug>/` | `src/gzkit/chores/<slug>/` (canonical class only) | none | none |

Sync compares no versions: it rewrites every mirror from canon, so a hand edit to a mirror is lost at the next sync. The drift report is `gz validate --surfaces`: *"Generated surface is out of sync with canonical state. Run `uv run gz agent sync control-surfaces` to repair."* (`validate_pkg/sync_parity.py`). Before running that sync, carry any mirror edit worth keeping into `.gzkit/` and bump its version; flag one whose origin is unclear for human review. Full resolution design: [Skill-Surface-Sync Rationale](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md).

## Bootstrap semantics (`gz init`)

After `gz init`, the adopter's `.gzkit/<surface>/` is the canonical source and rule 1 binds from then on; the wheel's package surface is the one-time bootstrap source. Repair-mode `gz init` is idempotent (`skip_existing=True`); `--force` wipes and re-copies. Retired-slug filtering, scaffolding order and the `gz init --update` roadmap: [Rationale § Bootstrap semantics](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md#bootstrap-semantics-gz-init).

## Retirement policy (delete-on-retire, binding)

A superseded or consolidated skill's directory is deleted from every surface root — `.gzkit/skills/`, `src/gzkit/skills/`, each enabled vendor's `<surface_root>/skills/` — in the same commit or OBPI that introduces its successor. No `lifecycle_state: retired` stub survives. Rationale (GHI #464): [Rationale § Retirement policy](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md#retirement-policy-delete-on-retire).

A retired rule leaves the same way. Its doctrine moves first, to a named home: a skill that runs when the rule binds, a doc under `docs/governance/`, an `AGENTS.md` entry, or the failure message of the witness that enforces it. Retiring never deletes doctrine. In the commit that retires the rule:

- delete `.gzkit/rules/<name>.md`, then sync, which removes the vendor mirrors. Sync never removes the package copy, so delete `src/gzkit/rules/<name>.md` by hand. That is the one exception to rule 5, and it lasts until GHI #1316 lands;
- remove its entry from `data/distribution_baseline_manifest.json` and its row from the Coverage Ledger of `docs/governance/advisory-rules-audit.md`, and re-point or retire the scorecard rows that cite it;
- re-point every test, validator message, doc link and `.gzkit/chores/registry.json` target that names the rule's path.

A test behind an attested REQ that reads the rule is repaired at the surface (`AGENTS.md` § OBPI Acceptance Protocol, attested REQ whose subject a later ruling retired); one whose REQ asserts the file exists goes to the operator first. **Advisory in part:** `gz validate --distribution` refuses a baseline entry left behind, but sync never removes the package copy (GHI #1316) or an adopter's copy, and no witness flags an orphaned ledger row (GHI #1317).

## Canonical surface class-classifier

Every file under a canonical surface (`src/gzkit/{chores,rules,skills,personas,templates}/`) is exactly one class (OBPI-0.0.32-13/-15):

| Class | Definition | Byte-parity | Sync |
|---|---|---|---|
| **canonical** | operator-authored content present at `.gzkit/<surface>/` | required | `.gzkit/ → src/gzkit/`; in the wheel and the baseline manifest |
| **package_only** | Python modules and support files with no `.gzkit/` counterpart (`__init__.py`, `_scaffolder.py`), and a retired skill the wheel still carries | exempt | never propagated to `.gzkit/` |
| **runtime_state** | per-run logs, receipts, proofs | exempt | never synced either way |
| **project_local** *(chores and skills)* | a chore whose `registry.json` entry declares `"projectLocal": true`, or a skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter declares `project_local: true` (GHI #915) | exempt | never shipped in the wheel or scaffolded by `gz init` |

Declare a project-local chore with `"projectLocal": true` in `.gzkit/chores/registry.json`, and a project-local skill with `project_local: true` in its `SKILL.md` frontmatter — the property is declared, never inferred, and the shipped `registry.json` is filtered so the wheel never advertises a chore it does not carry (GHI #728). `gz validate --distribution` and `sync_pkg_surfaces` both read the per-surface `_classify_<surface>_file` helpers. Per-surface default classes and the classifier matrix: [Rationale § Class-classifier reference](../../docs/governance/skill-surface-sync-rationale.md#class-classifier-reference).

# Tool / Skill / Runbook Alignment

> **Rule version:** `0.5.4` — § Enforcement posture says `--skill-alignment` and `--cli-alignment` are explicit-only, reachable from no gate (operator, 2026-11-08: *"fix what is stale"*); version narrative in [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#tool-skill-runbook-alignmentmd).

gzkit's operator surface is a three-layer hierarchy: **tools** (CLI verbs), **skills** (operator-facing value chains composing tools toward an intent), and **runbooks** (documentation preserving operator intent across iteration). These three invariants are the mechanical test for layer alignment; apply them whenever you author or modify any of the three surfaces.

## Invariants

### Invariant 1 — Every CLI tool has at least one skill that wields it

Every CLI verb registered in `src/gzkit/cli/` must be invoked by at least one skill under `.gzkit/skills/` — either via the skill's frontmatter `gz_command:` field or in the skill's body instructions. An orphaned tool (a live CLI verb with no skill pointing at it) is either dead code or hidden drift — either way, it is a defect signal.

### Invariant 2 — Every skill's `gz_command` matches a runbook-prescribed tool for the same operator moment

Every skill's declared `gz_command:` (frontmatter or body) must resolve to a CLI verb that the runbook prescribes for the same operator moment. If the skill name and its actual CLI target describe different operator moments — or if the skill invokes a verb the runbook does not prescribe for that moment — the skill is drifted from the runbook's preserved intent.

### Invariant 3 — Destination verb's default output form must honor the routing skill's Output Contract

When a skill's Output Contract declares a required rendering form ("table", "JSON", "tree", "plain text", etc.), the CLI verb in the skill's `gz_command` must produce that form as its default human-readable output. If the skill promises a table and the verb emits prose, the skill is drifted from its destination regardless of whether the verb name matches (Invariant 2). Invariant 3 closes the gap between "right verb routed" and "right rendering produced."

## Enforcement posture

**Invariant 1 has a validator that runs only on request. Invariants 2 and 3 are
advisory, and that is the settled disposition rather than a queue.**
`gz validate --skill-alignment` (GHI #202) checks Invariant 1 by scanning every
registered CLI verb path, multi-word subcommands included (GHI #588), and
requiring a wielding skill under `.gzkit/skills/**`, with explicit waivers in
`_NO_SKILL_VERBS`. The scope is explicit-only: no `gz check` step, hook, CI
workflow or pre-commit entry runs it (`data/validator_reachability_grandfather.json`),
so an orphaned verb lands green unless someone runs the scope. It landed first
deliberately — to establish the waiver shape before the harder scans.

The two that remain unmechanized both turn on **"the same operator moment"**, and
that phrase is the obstacle, not the missing code. Nothing in the repository
represents an operator moment as a comparable object: the runbook prescribes
verbs in prose, and deciding whether a skill's `gz_command` and a runbook step
describe *the same* moment is a reading of intent. A checker would have to
compare two prose surfaces and score their agreement — grading by shape, which is
the `shape-graded-not-substance` signature ADR-0.0.73 refuses. Invariant 3 adds a
second unmodelled term: a verb's "default human-readable output form" is
observed by running it, and the Output Contract that must match is prose too.

What *is* checkable nearby: every `gz <verb>` string in an operator-facing doc
must resolve to a registered parser verb (`gz validate --cli-alignment`, per
`AGENTS.md` § Governance doctrine surfaces, verb resolution). It fails closed
when run, but it too is explicit-only and reachable from no gate, so it catches
the renamed-verb half of Invariant 2 — a reference pointing at a verb that does
not exist — only when someone runs it. The same-moment judgment stays
unenforced.

Reclassify on named, observed evidence: a skill routed to a live verb that was
the *wrong* verb for its moment, or a skill whose promised rendering the verb did
not produce, that shipped and was caught late. Under the § Recommended promotion
order freeze in `docs/governance/advisory-rules-audit.md` (2026-06-08,
opt-in-with-justification), the absence of such an instance is a reason not to
build the checker.

## When to apply

- **Authoring a new CLI verb** — the wielding skill is **one of seven** obligations that fire together; `.gzkit/rules/cli.md` § Adding CLI Features — New Subcommand is the authority and this list deliberately does not restate it. Ensure a skill wields the verb in the authoring patch, or use the existing explicit waiver route with rationale. Filing a follow-up GHI does not satisfy this obligation.
- **Renaming a CLI verb** — audit every referencing skill (frontmatter `gz_command:` + body invocations); update in same patch
- **Authoring a new skill** — confirm `gz_command:` target matches the runbook-prescribed verb for that operator moment, and run the target once to verify output form matches Output Contract
- **Renaming a skill** — confirm `gz_command:` still aligns with the new name's implied operator moment
- **Re-routing a skill's `gz_command`** — run the new target and observe default output before committing; fix destination verb or skill contract if form disagrees
- **Editing the runbook** — confirm prescribed verbs still match skill-layer routing; add missing skills or update prescriptions
- **Editing a CLI verb's rendering** — check every skill whose `gz_command` points at that verb; preserve any Output Contract-declared form

> See [`docs/governance/tool-skill-runbook-rationale.md`](../../docs/governance/tool-skill-runbook-rationale.md) for canonical violation examples, enforcement details, commit-message discipline, and rationale.
